- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day) and sentiment is neutral or negative, expect sharp reversal; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >1.5% from peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and model is overconfident (high forecast variance), reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with pessimism.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 7–10 days if sentiment is weak or mixed.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match sentiment swing direction 1–2 days ahead.
